text.text_excerpt: Just ate at several truly excellent restaurants in NOLA (Cochon, Stella!, Luke, Herbsaint, Patois) over 5 days and, for my money, the single best one was Lilette. The food is very creative and prepared meticulously, the wait staff is excellent, and the ambience is nearly perfect. This restaurant could be dropped into LA, SF, Seattle, Boston, etc. and it would compare favorably with their best. Yes, it's that good. We had a 9:15pm reservation on a Friday night and snuck in a bit early, although things were still very busy. The single room is very pretty and laid out in a Parisian bistro fashion, meaning you're not going to get a lot of elbow room. Not a problem, just cozy. The wine list he...

In terms of food - this is one of the best you can get in New Orleans, really. Came here on a Thursday night last week - the restaurant is located in a cute building on the always trendy Magazine street - street parking is easy to find. Inside is a small, intimate dining room with the walls maroon and with large chalkboards dictating the specials and drinks. Only a few negative things I have to say before I start off about the positive - the specialty drinks are not very good. We each had a different specialty drink (mind you I can't remember what they were because we left the restaurant completely shitfaced) - but they were all each too bitter, too sweet, or too strong. We ate here some time ago with a fairly large group of friends for a special occasion. They were very accommodating for our table size and made sure to try and keep everyone taken care of as drinks ran out, bread was devoured, etc. Very intimate interior, which would be fantastic for a dinner date. Service as previously mentioned was impeccable and very friendly. Food was superb. They have a large daily special chalkbaord that had some amazing offerings on top of an already exciting menu. Food runs fairly rich and will definitely fill you up for your buck. For the most part, the fare is french, more so than french creole, and well plated.
